_comment: Adds the HCF register's facilities that had no site record, where an operator's own
page places them: ADC Mitchell and Fyshwick, NEXTDC B1 and B2, Fujitsu Western Sydney
and Homebush Bay, Polaris, Macquarie IC3 East. hcf_certified is left to
hcf_register.json, which loads next and fills it with the register's line quoted.
Five facilities are held as RG-101 rather than guessed at; missing fields on the new
rows are RG-103; the IC3 Super West contradiction is RG-104 and changes no value.

entities.name: Australian Data Centres
entities.notes: Australian-owned colocation and build-to-suit provider. Its own page: 'Continuous Canberra operations since 2014' and 'More than 10 years continuous operation at Mitchell and Fyshwick in Canberra ACT'. The page also describes 'Strategic development of a 300MW+ AI-optimised Melbourne campus in accelerated planning', which is a lead for a future site record, not a fact recorded here.

entities.name: Polaris Data Centre
entities.notes: Operator of the Polaris facility at Springfield Central, Queensland, on its own page. The Commonwealth HCF register names Springfield Real Estate Sales Pty Ltd as the certified service provider for Polaris Data Centre; how that entity relates to the Springfield City Group that owns the facility is not stated on the page (RG-103).

entities.name: Springfield City Group
entities.notes: Polaris Data Centre's own page: 'Polaris is 100% owned by the Springfield City Group, a 100% Queensland-owned business.' Recorded as the facility's owner.

sites.name: ADC Mitchell (Australian Data Centres)
sites.notes: Australian Data Centres' own page: 'More than 10 years continuous operation at Mitchell and Fyshwick in Canberra ACT'; its locations page lists 'Operational – Canberra (Mitchell, Fyshwick)'. The Commonwealth HCF register lists ADC Mitchell as a Certified Strategic Facility (quoted on this row). Neither page states an address, a site area or a capacity, so none is recorded - RG-103. The operator also describes a 300MW+ AI-optimised Melbourne campus in accelerated planning; that is a separate, unlocated proposal and is not recorded as a site.

sites.name: ADC Fyshwick (Australian Data Centres)
sites.notes: Australian Data Centres' own page: 'More than 10 years continuous operation at Mitchell and Fyshwick in Canberra ACT'; its locations page lists 'Operational – Canberra (Mitchell, Fyshwick)'. The Commonwealth HCF register lists ADC Fyshwick as a Certified Strategic Enclave (quoted on this row). Neither page states an address, a site area or a capacity, so none is recorded - RG-103. A different provider's facilities in the same suburb: CDC's Fyshwick F1 and F2 are recorded under SITE_CDC_CANBERRA and are not this facility.

sites.name: NEXTDC B1 Brisbane
sites.notes: NEXTDC's own B1 page: 'Located in Brisbane's CBD, B1 Brisbane is a 2.25MW data centre designed and built to Uptime Institute Tier III standards', labelled '2.25MW IT Capacity'; its portfolio table gives 1,650m² of technical space (not gross floor area, so no area field is filled). The HCF register lists Brisbane 1 as a Certified Strategic Enclave. No street address is published on the page - RG-103.

sites.name: NEXTDC B2 Brisbane
sites.notes: NEXTDC's own B2 page: 'Located in Fortitude Valley on the fringe of the Brisbane CBD, B2 Brisbane is a 12MW Tier IV certified data centre', labelled '12MW IT Capacity', 6,000m² in its portfolio table. The 12 MW recorded here is the facility's IT capacity as the operator states it, not delivered capacity: NEXTDC's FY26 results presentation (27 August 2026) reports 'Built capacity 6MW built, 2MW in progress' against 'Total power planned 12MW'. The HCF register lists Brisbane 2 as a Certified Strategic Enclave. No street address is published on the page - RG-103.

sites.name: Fujitsu Western Sydney Data Centre
sites.notes: Fujitsu's own release of 30 September 2020 lists its six Australian facilities: 'Homebush Bay, Western Sydney, and North Ryde in New South Wales; Noble Park in Victoria; Eight Mile Plains in Queensland; and Malaga in Western Australia'. The same release says further expansion phases would provide 'a combined total capacity of 90 megawatts at the Western Sydney data centre campus' - a 2020 end-state figure for the campus, not a current capacity, so no capacity field is filled (RG-103). The HCF register lists Western Sydney as a Certified Strategic Enclave. The release gives no suburb or street address for the campus.

sites.name: Fujitsu Homebush Bay Data Centre
sites.notes: The HCF register names this facility 'Homebush'. Fujitsu's own release of 30 September 2020 names 'Homebush Bay' among its six Australian facilities and lists no other Homebush facility; the two names are read as the same facility, which is why this row is REPORTED at medium confidence rather than VERIFIED. No address, area or capacity is stated - RG-103.

sites.name: Polaris Data Centre (Springfield Central)
sites.address: 11 Mary Mackenroth Lane, Springfield Central QLD 4300
sites.notes: Polaris's own page: 'Queensland’s largest, 100% Australian owned data centre', 'Located in Springfield, 25km from Brisbane’s CBD', address in its footer. It describes 'over 14,500m2 over 5 levels, with over 7,000m2 of raised technical floor space': both are lower bounds and technical space is not gross floor area, so no area field is filled. No capacity is published. The HCF register certifies Polaris Data Centre as a Strategic Enclave under Springfield Real Estate Sales Pty Ltd; the page says the facility is 100% owned by the Springfield City Group. How those entities relate, and which one operates the facility, is RG-103.

sites.name: Macquarie IC3 East (Macquarie Park)
sites.notes: Macquarie Data Centres' own IC3 East page gives '12MW IT Load' and '11,700m2 Technical space' (technical space, not gross floor area, so no area field is filled), within what it calls its 65MW Macquarie Park campus. The HCF register lists IC3e as a Certified Strategic Enclave alongside IC1, IC2 and IC3. The campus's other building, IC3 Super West, is a separate facility and the subject of RG-104; this row is not a second record of it.

research_gaps.question: Where are the five HCF-certified facilities that still have no site record - Cloud Carrier DB1; DigiCo BNE2, ADL1 and SYD1; and Vocus TransACT House Dickson - who operates them, and what are their status and capacity?
research_gaps.why_it_matters: The register is the Commonwealth's own list of facilities cleared to host government data. Five of its entries are missing from the observatory, so the certified estate is under-counted and the sovereign-hosting map has holes in exactly the providers that are hardest to see.
research_gaps.target_source: Operators' own facility pages (cloudcarrier.com, digi-co.com.au, vocus.com.au); ABR/ASIC for the operating entities; the HCF register itself
research_gaps.notes: OPENED 2026-11-15 from the Commonwealth register (SRC_HCF_REGISTER). The register gives a provider and a facility name and nothing else - no jurisdiction, address, status or capacity - and sites.state and sites.status are required, so no row has been invented for these five: Cloud Carrier - DB1 (facility), register line 'Cloud Carrier – DB1'; DigiCo - BNE2 (facility), register line 'DigiCo – BNE2'; DigiCo - ADL1 (enclave), register line 'DigiCo – ADL1 and SYD1'; DigiCo - SYD1 (enclave), register line 'DigiCo – ADL1 and SYD1'; Vocus - TransACT House Dickson (enclave), register line 'Vocus - TransACT House Dickson'. Attempts to place them: https://www.digi-co.com.au/data-centres/ - robots.txt could not be read (refused), read as disallow-all (2026-11-16); https://cloudcarrier.com/ - robots.txt could not be read (refused), read as disallow-all (2026-11-16); https://cloudcarrier.com/about-us/ - robots.txt could not be read (refused), read as disallow-all (2026-11-16). Both refusals are recorded in data/raw/operators/<group>/refused.json and were not worked around. Vocus's own wholesale data centre page was archived (data/raw/operators/vocus/data-centres.txt): it sells connectivity into more than 150 data centres and names none of its own facilities, so it does not place TransACT House. DigiCo SYD1 needs care: SITE_DIGICO_SYD1 already records the SYD1 EXPANSION project from a NSW consent, while the register certifies an enclave in the existing facility. A new row must distinguish the two before it is created, or the record repeats the double-count RG-084 removed. Eight other register facilities were placed from operators' own pages and are added by this pack; their missing fields are RG-103.

research_gaps.question: Addresses, site areas and capacities for the eight facilities added from the HCF register (ADC Mitchell and Fyshwick, NEXTDC B1 and B2, Fujitsu Western Sydney and Homebush Bay, Polaris, Macquarie IC3 East), and which legal entity operates Polaris?
research_gaps.why_it_matters: These rows exist because the Commonwealth certifies them, not because a planning record places them. Without an address they cannot be mapped, matched to a consent, or checked for double-counting against the rows that came from the planning portal.
research_gaps.target_source: Operators' facility and contact pages; ABR/ASIC for Springfield Real Estate Sales Pty Ltd and the Springfield City Group; NSW/QLD/ACT planning registers
research_gaps.notes: OPENED 2026-11-15. What the archived pages do and do not state: Australian Data Centres names Mitchell and Fyshwick and says both are operational, but publishes no address, area or capacity for either. NEXTDC's B1 and B2 pages give IT capacity (2.25 MW, 12 MW) and technical space (1,650 m², 6,000 m²) but no street address; B2's delivered capacity (6 MW built, 2 MW in progress) is from its FY26 presentation, not its facility page. Fujitsu's only archived document is a 30 September 2020 release: it places Western Sydney and Homebush Bay in NSW and gives a 90 MW end-state for the Western Sydney campus, which is six years old and is not a current capacity. Polaris publishes an address and lower-bound areas ('over 14,500m2', 'over 7,000m2') but no capacity, and its owner (Springfield City Group) is not the entity the register certifies (Springfield Real Estate Sales Pty Ltd). Macquarie's IC3 East page gives 12 MW IT load and 11,700 m² of technical space. No lower bound and no technical-space figure has been stored as a value.

research_gaps.question: Is SITE_MACQ_IC3 - recorded as 'IC3 Super West', operational, from a grade-C directory - the register's certified 'IC3', when Macquarie's own page says IC3 Super West is under construction with 47 MW of IT load?
research_gaps.why_it_matters: A facility recorded as operational that its operator says is still being built inflates the operating estate, and the register's IC3 and IC3e entries cannot be assigned to buildings until it is settled. Macquarie Park is the cluster where the record has already double-counted once (RG-084).
research_gaps.target_source: Macquarie Data Centres' IC3 Super West and IC3 East pages (archived); the HCF register; Macquarie Technology Group's ASX announcements
research_gaps.notes: OPENED 2026-11-15. Macquarie's own IC3 Super West page, read for this batch, says 'IC3 Super West is currently under construction with the entire end-state power secured', gives '47MW IT Load' and lists the facility as 'Coming Soon'. SITE_MACQ_IC3 is named 'IC3 Super West (Macquarie Park)' and recorded operational on SRC_CERTSTRAT, a grade-C directory. The register lists 'IC1, IC2, IC3 and IC3e' as Certified Strategic Enclaves; IC3 East is operational at 12 MW IT load and is added by this batch as SITE_MACQ_IC3E. Which building each register name denotes, and whether a facility under construction can hold Strategic certification, is for a human. NO VALUE IS CHANGED HERE: the page is quoted against the existing row so the contradiction is on the record, not resolved by an agent.
